The starting point

The original OnFees app

These are five screens from the live app before I changed anything. They show what students see today and what I set out to fix.

What I noticed: the app stores plenty of information, but nothing tells a student what needs attention first.

The problem

A profile card where a briefing should be

Students open OnFees to learn what needs attention right now, but the first screen spends its space on who they are.

34notifications collapsed into one “Attendance” row
3side-menu items, and Logout is the most colourful
0overall attendance figures anywhere in the app

How might we let students find attendance, deadlines and fees in seconds, with less effort?

Dashboard

From profile card to daily briefing

  • Email, division and roll number fill the first screen
  • Attendance is only a link to a report
  • Three dropdowns and collapsed semesters sit in a large card
  • A short greeting replaces the profile card
  • An attendance ring shows 80% with Present and Absent counts
  • Quick Actions give one-tap access to six features
  • Upcoming deadlines and a notice banner follow
  • Fee summary turns red when payment is due, with a Pay Now button

Profile details moved to their own screen, freeing the dashboard for what students check daily.

The system

Screens that give key tasks a home

The old app had no dedicated place for fees, timetable, assignments or notices. Each now has a screen, reachable in one tap from Quick Actions.

Outcome

From an app that displays records to one that prioritises them.

A student opening the redesigned app sees attendance, the next deadline, new notices and fees within the first screen, then reaches any other feature in one tap.
